pagerduty-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty alert: incident RD-1234 — elevated gateway 5xx rate detected. 90s avg 5xx = 4.5% (baseline ~0.1%). Affected services: inference-gateway, api-proxy. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /api/chat. First observed: 1803007860. Severity: P1. Link: https://ops.redwood/RD-1234

Alex Chen: I’m oncall. I see the spike in Grafana — error rate correlates with a latency increase on the gateway pods. Trying to fetch recent gateway logs now.

Mira Patel: I’m joining. Can someone confirm if this is client-side timeouts or upstream 5xx from runtime?

Alex Chen: Good question — quick tail from gateway (last 30 lines):
```
2026-03-14T15:07:40Z error request_id= status=502 upstream=runtime-01 path=/v1/generate msg="bad gateway: upstream read timeout"
2026-03-14T15:07:41Z error request_id= status=503 upstream=runtime-02 path=/v1/generate msg="upstream write failed: connection reset"
2026-03-14T15:07:42Z error request_id= status=504 upstream= path=/api/chat msg="no response from upstream"
```
Notably request_id is empty for some entries — observability gap.

Jin Park: I’m seeing high KV-cache thrash and GPU OOMs on runtime-02 from the metrics graph. But the runtimes are also reporting a surge of slow responses (p50 -> p95 jump).

Samir Das: Re: observability gap — our ingress should propagate X-Request-Id but looks like it’s not set for a subset of traffic (maybe from the LB). That makes tracing failures across services hard. Also our trace sampling dropped yesterday from 10% -> 0% due to a config roll.

Rachael Gomez (support): We already have two enterprise customers reporting errors in support. They see 502s in production UI — asking for ETA.

Mira Patel: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) increase gateway timeout to 90s, 2) scale runtime pool by +2, 3) enable fallback model variant for high-latency requests. Which ones can we do fast?

Alex Chen: I can scale gateway and bump timeout now. Jin, can you add 2 runtime replicas?

Jin Park: Adding replicas now — kubectl scale statefulset/runtime --replicas=6. Also increasing per-process heap limits on runtime-02 as a stopgap.

Samir Das: While scaling, we need stopgap instrumentation: inject temporary request_id at the gateway so logs correlate even if LB doesn’t. I can push a quick config to set `X-Request-Id` from a generated UUID when header missing. Also re-enable trace sampling to 5% immediately.

Alex Chen: Doing timeout bump:
```
kubectl patch deployment gateway -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"gateway","env":[{"name":"GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS","value":"90000"}]}]}}}}'
```
Patch applied. Confirming updated pods restarting.

Jin Park: Replicas converging to 6. One runtime pod reporting image pull error but others are up. p95 latency reduced slightly.

Samir Das: Pushed temporary middleware that sets X-Request-Id when missing and emits a lightweight metric `gateway.request_id_injected=1` with tags route, pod. Also turned trace sampler back on at 5%. Config diff:
```
- traces.sampler: 0.0
+ traces.sampler: 0.05
+ middleware: inject_request_id_if_missing=true
```
Metric appears in Datadog, I’ll add a dashboard quick panel.

Rachael Gomez (support): Pass to customers: We’ve applied infrastructure mitigations (scaled runtime + gateway timeout bump) and added extra logging/tracing — investigating root cause. Will update customers with a note: possible transient upstream resource pressure; ETA 30–45m for stability.

Mira Patel: Observed immediate effect: 5xx dropped from 4.5% -> 1.2% in last 60s window after scaling and instrumentation. However some 503s persist tied to runtime-02. Jin — please isolate runtime-02 for deeper debugging and failover traffic away.

Jin Park: Redirecting traffic: adding a node selector to avoid runtime-02 host and cordoning the node for investigation. Command: `kubectl cordon node-runtime-02-host` then remove pod from service endpoints.

Alex Chen: Handoff: I’ll stay as primary until this is resolved. Mira, take secondary watch. Samir, continue to monitor logs/trace attach. Rachael please queue customer updates every 30m.

Samir Das: Noted. I’m collecting a sample set of requests that had empty request_id and will backfill logs with the injected UUID where possible. Also creating a quick synthetic check to ensure the LB is passing headers — if not we’ll escalate to infra.

Mira Patel: Postmortem notes (to capture while fresh):
- Impact: 4.5% error rate at peak, affecting realtime chat/generation; some enterprise customers impacted.
- Root cause hypothesis: abrupt resource pressure on runtime-02 (KV cache thrash + OOM) amplified by missing request_id and trace sampling misconfig, making live debugging slow.
- Observability gaps: missing request_id in gateway logs, trace sampler config rollback, no lightweight request-level metric for injected IDs.
- Short-term fixes: inject request_id at gateway, re-enable traces, scale runtimes, cordon problematic node, increase timeouts.
- Long-term actions: make X-Request-Id mandatory at LB, automated rollback guard on trace sampler config, add an SLO alert for trace sampling rate, add runtime OOM early-warning metric.

Alex Chen: Confirming last check: 5xx down to 0.4% and p95 latency improving. Keeping incident open for monitoring. Next update in 20m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident RD-1234 status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned: Alex Chen (primary). Link: https://ops.redwood/RD-1234

Rachael Gomez (support): Thanks team — I’ll send external note that mitigations are in place and we’re monitoring.

Mira Patel: Filing this as a high-priority postmortem, including the quick instrumentation diffs Samir pushed. Please drop any logs/traces samples in the incident doc.

Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. If anyone sees a regression ping me @alex or update this thread.
